shared_elements: monolithic standing pillar carved in low relief
schematic animal/creature forms rendered in shallow relief
horizontal band or belt-like division across the body of the stone
stacked registers of motifs on a vertical surface
suggestion of arms or limbs carved on the stone body
justification: Both are anthropomorphising standing pillars whose surfaces carry shallow, highly schematic relief organised into stacked zones, with a horizontal band or belt dividing an upper zone of repeated creature-like motifs from a lower zone, and both include a disc and sinuous serpentine forms. The difference is in the specific content: A shows a clear menagerie of identifiable profile animals (quadrupeds, long-necked birds, insect-like creature) arranged as a narrative-like assemblage, whereas B's carving is dominated by a single anthropomorphic body with a face/headdress, arms and belt, with only faint ornamental motifs rather than a bestiary.
